title: Migration header says erasure 'removes the row' while the same file's erased_at tombstone keeps it
evidence:
+--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
+--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.
...
+  -- Erasure tombstone: a confirmed Art. 17 deletion wipes fields/token but
+  -- keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close so a still-open form
detail: Header comment documents row deletion; the erased_at column comment (and the spec's W3 'tombstone-not-delete' ruling) documents row retention as a suppression record. GDPR-erasure semantics stated two contradictory ways in one file.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the header bullet to describe the tombstone: fields/token wiped, erased_at set, (vacancy,email) kept as suppression record until vacancy close.

title: Spec says the serializer skips hidden inputs; shouldSkipControl never checks type 'hidden'
detail: The claimed hidden-skip exists only via the underscore-prefix naming convention. Any present or future hidden input without a '_' prefix is silently persisted into draft PII, and no test pins hidden exclusion.
recommended_fix: Add an explicit `if (type === "hidden") return true;` to shouldSkipControl and a serializer test pinning that hidden controls never leave the page.

title: Suggested Review Order still points reviewers at 'data-resume-token', which round 3 removed from the DOM
evidence:
+  Blocker (autocapture leak): the resume token no longer sits in ANY DOM
+  attribute — PostHog autocapture reads element attributes into
vs
+- Marker, banner, data-resume-token, backdated timing stamp.
+  [`form_pages.gleam:387`](../../server/src/application/form_pages.gleam#L387)
detail: Round 3 moved the token to window.__rtResumeToken precisely because a DOM attribute leaked into autocapture, yet the review-order section (current guidance, not changelog history) still names data-resume-token.
recommended_fix: Update the review-order bullet to reference the CSP-nonced inline global (window.__rtResumeToken) instead of data-resume-token.

title: Spec task checklist schema omits erased_at and still describes erasure as delete_by_token
evidence:
+- [x] `supabase/migrations/<ts>_create_application_draft.sql` — `application_draft(id uuid PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), vacancy_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vacancy(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, email text NOT NULL, fields jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', continue_token text NULL, last_link_sent_at timestamptz NULL, resumed_at timestamptz NULL, submitted_at timestamptz NULL, created_at/updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE(vacancy_id, email))`
vs
+  erased_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
detail: The execution checklist's canonical schema was never updated after the W3 tombstone ruling; the shipped migration carries erased_at. Checklist and artifact disagree on the table definition.
recommended_fix: Amend the task line to include erased_at and rename delete_by_token to reflect the tombstone (wipe + stamp) semantics.

title: 'Copy pins (sync with form_copy.gleam)' test pins only the JS half — Gleam drift fails nothing
evidence:
+// ---------- Copy pins (sync with form_copy.gleam) ----------
...
+  // Applicant-facing copy — KEEP IN SYNC with server/src/application/
+  // form_copy.gleam (same precedent as REVIEW_HINT_STEPPER in
detail: The test name claims a cross-language sync guarantee, but it can only assert the JS constants. A form_copy.gleam edit passes everything while the applicant-facing strings diverge.
recommended_fix: Either rename the test to drop the sync claim, or add a server-side test asserting the Gleam constants equal these strings (grep-based or fixture).

title: Capability gate checks fetch/CustomEvent/JSON but the continue-click chain uses Promise.prototype.finally
detail: Browsers with fetch but without Promise.finally (older Edge/Safari) pass the gate, then the click handler throws constructing the chain and the button stays disabled with no status copy.
recommended_fix: Replace .finally with a .then pair (or add finally to the gate) so the button re-enables on every browser the gate admits.

title: saveNow learns nothing from non-2xx: oversize (413) payloads retry on every step change and pagehide forever
detail: The closed-vacancy answer terminally disables the saver, but a terminally-unsaveable payload (over 64 KB, over key/value caps) just falls through silently and is re-POSTed on every subsequent step change and tab close.
recommended_fix: Treat repeated non-2xx saves as terminal for the current payload (disable until the payload changes), or client-side pre-check the 64 KB/key caps before sending.
